key_insight: Boron redistributes toward defects in TiAl, locally pinning dislocations and suppressing deformation twinning to strengthen the alloy at high temperature.
engineering_relevance: Controlling boron content and defect structure could improve high-temperature TiAl strength, while brittle borides and interface-dependent adhesion require careful management.
method: Develop a high-fidelity machine-learning interatomic potential.
Simulate boron redistribution using hybrid grand-canonical Monte Carlo/molecular dynamics.
Analyze defect interactions, tensile deformation, and stacking-fault energetics.
evidence_signal: Polycrystalline TiAl simulations show a 9.4% increase in average flow stress at 1 at.% B and 900 K, accompanied by reduced shear strain accumulation.
watch_item: The strengthening result is simulation-based; experimental validation and transferability across alloy compositions and processing conditions remain important.
paper_title: Atomistic insight into defect-mediated boron redistribution and high-temperature strengthening in TiAl alloys
